newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo says army involved in recent killings.
newsitem.headline: New Congo says army involved in recent killings.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's soldiers were involved in recent killings in the Democratic Congo capital Kinshasa, authorities said on Thursday.
Interior Minister Mwenze Kongolo told a news conference investigations were continuing into Sunday night's killing of at least 13 people in the city, but added:
"With certainty, we know that four people are involved in the killings. Some elements of our army are also involved. The public is entitled to know these things."
The minister said suspects would be paraded before the general public in the next few days.
The crime rate in Kinshasa has soared since Kabila overthrew veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko in May after a seven-month guerrilla campaign.
However an official statement read out on state radio last Monday absolved Kabila's Alliance forces from blame.
"A group of armed criminals claiming to be members of the Alliance forces are committing many crimes. The police will finally track them down," it said.
Mwenze pursued that line on Thursday by saying it was not clear who was in the army and who was not. He said there were people in military uniform who were not Alliance soldiers.
"Our army has been infiltrated. Our task is not easy. In a short time we will identify the soldiers in town and determine their units," he said.
He declined to say whether the alleged infiltrators were members of Mobutu's defeated army.
The security situation has been compounded by public reaction to the rising crime wave.
Thieves and house-breakers caught red-handed have been lynched or burned to death. The interim governor of Kinshasa has vowed to punish anyone resorting to "private justice".
It was not immediately clear whether those killed on Sunday night were suspected criminals or robbery victims.
Gunmen routinely cruise the streets of the city of over five million people in stolen cars, shooting in the air.
Mwenze said the army planned to seal off some residential areas of Kinshasa, in an attempt to disarm civilians.
"There are too many weapons in this city," he said.
